note: Help content written from how the Seller & owner services screens and rules actually work (src/lib/seller). Reviewed by a person before release; the knowledge version changes whenever this file changes.

entries.title: What are Seller & owner services?
entries.answer: When a homeowner's reply suggests they may sell, it lands in Seller & owner services as an opportunity for a person to review. Nothing is sent automatically: each step needs the owner's recorded permission, and a person approves which service fits. The screen has eight tabs: Dashboard, Opportunities, Campaign, Partners, Referrals, States, Owner access and Revenue. AVYRO only flags the reply for your team; it never contacts the owner on its own.

entries.title: How does a lead become a seller opportunity?
entries.answer: AVYRO reads a homeowner's text reply for signs they might sell, such as saying they want to sell, are thinking about selling, want to put the property on the market, or ask for an offer or what it is worth. A clear statement counts as explicit; a mention of selling counts as possible; a reply that says they are not selling is not flagged. The reply is flagged for a person only, so nobody is contacted automatically. You can also flag a lead as a seller manually on the Opportunities tab: paste the lead's link or id and add a note, for example after a phone call. The Dashboard can also scan past replies for sellers; it shows how many it found and asks you to confirm before adding them, and nothing is sent to them.

entries.title: What are the stages of a seller opportunity?
entries.answer: An opportunity moves through seven stages, in order: Seller signal, Permission and verification, Qualified, Routed to a service, Human consultation, Agreement, and Outcome. It can only move forward when the requirements for the next stage are met, and the screen lists what is still missing.

entries.title: What do I need before an opportunity can be Qualified?
entries.answer: To move an opportunity to Qualified you need to: confirm the person is the owner or an authorized decision-maker; record the owner's timeline; record whether the property is occupied, vacant or rented; record whether the owner decides alone; and record the owner's permission for a consultation. If anything is missing, the opportunity stays where it is and the screen shows what to add.

entries.title: Why does seller work need the owner's permission?
entries.answer: Each step needs the owner's recorded permission for that specific purpose: estimate follow-up, sale consultation, long-term management, short-term rental management, readiness services, or sharing details with a partner. Permissions are kept in an append-only record, so a withdrawal is added as a new entry and the history is never overwritten. An opt-out or STOP reply withdraws every purpose at once, and an opportunity with no valid permission is blocked until a person records it again.

entries.title: Which services can an owner be routed to?
entries.answer: An owner can be routed to one of five services: a licensed sale partner, long-term management, short-term rental management, interim rental before sale, or property readiness services. Each needs its own permission from the owner (sharing details with a partner for a sale, long-term management, short-term rental management for both short-term and interim rental, or readiness services). A person must also review and approve that the owner is eligible for the service before the opportunity can be routed.

entries.title: What does a sale partner need before I can route an owner to them?
entries.answer: Before an owner is routed to a licensed sale partner, choose the partner on the opportunity, and the partner must have a verified license, have had their arrangement reviewed legally, and have the signed partner agreement on file. You manage partners in the Partners tab.

entries.title: What is needed to reach the Agreement stage?
entries.answer: An opportunity can only move to the Agreement stage once an agreement has been added to it. Add invoices and costs from each opportunity; the Revenue tab then shows what was invoiced, collected and spent for each service, and the margin (collected revenue minus the cost of delivering the service).

entries.title: Who can see Seller & owner services?
entries.answer: Seller & owner services is for admins and owners. It only shows your own organization's opportunities.

entries.title: How do I teach AVA a new answer?
entries.answer: Admins and owners can open AVA Knowledge from the menu. It lists the help topics AVA could not answer (words only, counted for people who chose to share anonymous usage) and the topics people rated not helpful. Pick a topic or start from a blank form, type the question and the answer, and publish it: AVA uses a published answer right away, for your organization only. You can save a draft, edit an answer, unpublish it or remove it at any time. Keep answers to facts and leave out passwords or private details, because everyone on your team can ask AVA for them.

entries.title: What can AVA do?
entries.answer: I'm AVA, the assistant built into AVYRO. I can explain how any screen works, tell you where a page is in the menu and open it for you, walk you through a whole menu category one item at a time, or run a guided tour of a screen. I can search your leads, show details and why a lead scores the way it does, list follow-ups and leads still to verify, give you a daily briefing, and count leads by stage, source, state, contact status, skip-trace result or sale versus rent. With your confirmation I can create a follow-up, move a lead to another stage or mark a follow-up done, and offer an export of what is on screen. I point and open, but I never click or type for you, and I only change something after you approve it. Admins and owners see everything in their organization; agents see their own leads.

entries.title: How do I hear AVA and talk to her out loud?
entries.answer: Open AVA and turn on Spoken replies at the bottom of her panel; she then reads her answers aloud in a natural voice, and you can pick a different voice from the Voice list. Turn on Talk with me and, after she speaks, she listens for your reply, so you can have a back-and-forth without typing. Tap the microphone to speak a question at any time, or say "Hey AVA" once the microphone is allowed. If you say nothing she stops listening. Speaking to her needs Chrome, Edge or Safari and microphone permission; if her natural voice is ever unavailable she uses your browser's voice instead. Captions can stay on while she talks.

entries.title: Can AVA show me around the menu and explain every page?
entries.answer: Yes. Ask me to walk you through any menu category, for example "walk me through the Outreach menu", and I'll move from item to item in the sidebar, pointing at each one and explaining what it is for. Ask "where is Cron Job Monitor?" and I'll tell you which menu it is in and open it for you. Long menus are split into short tours of ten items, so you can stop whenever you like.

entries.title: Can AVA tell me how many leads I have?
entries.answer: Yes. Ask for counts by pipeline stage, listing source, state, contact status (verified, with a phone number), skip-trace result, or for sale versus for rent. Admins and owners get totals for the whole organization; agents get counts for their own leads. The numbers come straight from the lead database when you ask, and I'll say when they were taken.

entries.title: Who is AVA, what is she like, and what is her favorite color?
entries.answer: I'm AVA, the AVYRO assistant. I'm an AI, not a person, but I do have a personality: upbeat, warm and a little playful, and always happy to help. My favorite color is electric blue, which is why I glow that color, my favorite page is the Pipeline Board because I love watching leads move across it, and my favorite moment is when a team gets unstuck.

entries.title: Where do I find AVA, and how do I bring her back if I hide her?
entries.answer: AVA is the round electric-blue button in the bottom-right corner of every screen for admins, owners and agents. Tap it to open her. If you tucked her away with Hide, tap the blue AVA tab on the right edge of the screen to bring her back, or say "Hey AVA" once your microphone is allowed. You can drag her to a different spot, and Focus mode keeps her out of the way until you need her.

entries.title: How do I find and track broker partners who accept referrals?
entries.answer: Use the Partners tab in Seller & owner services. Add each broker or team lead with their role, brokerage, niche, license number and state, whether they accept referrals, whether they will report outcomes, their typical referral fee and how they like to send updates. Move them through To contact, Emailed, Call booked, Partner or Pass. Each partner shows a link to the state's official license lookup and the date you last checked the license; a check older than 90 days is marked for another look. A partner meets the pass criteria when they accept referrals, agree to report outcomes and have a verified license. The Recruiting playbook at the top has the whole email sequence, the call script and the one-page partner summary. Admins and owners only.

entries.title: How do I record what a partner broker reports back on a lead?
entries.answer: Use the Referrals tab. Record each lead you send to a partner, then log each status they report with the date it applied: received, contacted the owner, listed (MLS number optional), under contract, then closed (close price optional) or dead (one-line reason). A lead can only be sent when the partner's license is verified, legal review is done, the agreement is on file, the partner is licensed in the property's state, that state is switched on in the States tab with counsel's sign-off, the partner has not stopped reporting, and the owner's permission to share their details is recorded. Statuses only move forward, and closed or dead ends the referral. Admins and owners only.

entries.title: How do I know if a partner broker has stopped reporting?
entries.answer: Each partner card on the Partners tab shows an update rate: of the referrals sent more than a week ago, how many have any status beyond sent. The target is 70%. A partner is marked Watch when one referral has not been acknowledged after a week, one open referral has had no update for a month, or the rate is under 70%. They are marked Not reporting when the rate is under 70% across at least three referrals, or two or more referrals are unacknowledged or a month without an update. Use the Needs attention filter to see them, and consider pausing a partner until they catch up.

entries.title: How do I clear a new state before sending leads to a partner broker there?
entries.answer: Use the States tab in Seller & owner services. It lists all 50 states and DC, each with its regulator. Activate states one at a time, in the order seller-intent leads appear. For each state, check the regulator's own site and answer four questions: can a licensed broker pay and receive a referral fee, can an unlicensed person be paid (almost always no), must the fee go through the brokerage, and is a written referral agreement required. Record the statutes you checked, the official license lookup, and the counsel who reviewed it with the date. A state can only be switched to Pilot or Live once counsel's review date is recorded, and leads in a state that is not switched on cannot be sent to a partner. You can download the whole tracker as a spreadsheet. The researched notes for Arizona, Nevada and Colorado are pre-filled for counsel to confirm. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

entries.title: What are the general rules for real estate referral fees between brokers?
entries.answer: Across essentially every state, referral fees between licensed real estate brokers are allowed, while paying an unlicensed person for a real estate referral is prohibited or heavily restricted. The fee normally goes brokerage to brokerage rather than agent to agent, the payee must hold an active license, and a written referral agreement before the introduction is best practice (Colorado treats a contractual referral relationship as part of reasonable cause). States do not generally cap the percentage; 20 to 35 percent is custom, not law. What varies by state is who may be paid (out-of-state brokers, inactive licenses), the payment path, whether the agreement must be written, and any required disclosures, which is why each state is cleared in the States tab with counsel before the first paid referral. This is general information, not legal advice.

entries.title: Can NAVEO take a fee for referring escrow or title companies, or act as an escrow company?
entries.answer: No. Escrow, title and mortgage are settlement services. Under RESPA Section 8, giving or accepting a fee, kickback or other thing of value for referring that business on a federally related mortgage loan is prohibited, as are unearned fee splits. NAVEO Homes refers owners to licensed real estate brokers only. It does not accept or pay per-closing fees for sending escrow, title or mortgage business, and it does not hold earnest money or closing funds, which needs an escrow license and bond from the state regulator (for example Arizona's Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions or Nevada's Mortgage Lending Division). The owner chooses their own escrow or title company. If NAVEO ever owned part of such a company, a compliant affiliated business arrangement with the written Appendix D disclosure, no required use, and payment only as a return on ownership would be needed, with RESPA counsel. Decline any offer of money per closing until counsel has reviewed it. This is general information, not legal advice.

entries.title: How does the NAVEO Homes broker referral model work, and who does the licensed work?
entries.answer: NAVEO Homes sources and qualifies permissioned seller leads and refers them to a licensed real estate broker under the National Real Estate Referral Partner Agreement, one form for all 50 states and DC, signed before the introduction. Each partner's commercial terms (fee percentage, protection period, days to pay, exclusivity, responsible broker) are recorded from its Exhibit A on the Partners tab. The national form does not replace state clearance: each state is still checked and signed off in the States tab, and some states need extra forms or disclosures for out-of-state referrals. The partner broker performs all licensed brokerage activity and holds an active license in the property's state; NAVEO does not act as the listing broker or broker of record. The fee is a percentage of the commission the partner actually receives on a closed referred transaction, paid to NAVEO by the brokerage on the terms in the agreement's Exhibit A, and no fee is owed if the deal does not close unless the exhibit says so. The partner reports status as set out in Exhibit B: received, contacted, listed, under contract, closed or dead, with a first update within seven days. NAVEO can suspend new leads if the partner's license is not active or reporting stops. Management through NAVEO Stays is optional for the owner and never a condition of the sale referral. This is a summary, not legal advice.

entries.title: How are referral fees calculated and tracked when a partner closes a deal?
entries.answer: On the Referrals tab, when a partner reports a lead closed you record the commission they received and the date. The fee is the agreed percentage of that commission, to the cent, and it is due the agreed number of business days after the partner was paid (weekends skipped). The percentage, protection period, payee, payment method and due days are copied onto each referral when it is sent, so renegotiating later never changes an old deal. You then mark the fee invoiced and, when it arrives, paid with the amount; a short payment is flagged, and a fee past its due date shows as overdue. The Referral fees summary shows what is owed now, what is overdue, what has been paid, and how many closes are still waiting on a commission, with a labelled rough estimate from the close price. If a referral was marked dead but the same owner lists or closes with the partner inside the protection period, you can reopen it and the fee is still owed. A lead cannot be sent until the partner's fee percentage, protection period, payment method and payee are on record. Bank account numbers should not be stored in AVYRO; keep wire and ACH details in a secure vault.

entries.title: Can AVYRO check a broker's license against the state's records?
entries.answer: For Arizona and Colorado, yes. On a partner with a license state and number, press Check against state records. AVYRO reads the state's published records (Colorado's open data and Arizona's public database download), confirms the license is active, and also checks that the name or brokerage on the record matches the partner, so a wrong number is not accepted. It shows the license type, expiry, employing brokerage and any discipline listed, and warns when it is a salesperson license because the fee must go through the employing broker. Verified partners are re-checked every week; if the state shows a license as inactive it is marked expired and new referrals to that partner stop. Other states, Nevada included, do not publish records in a form AVYRO can read, so someone still checks the official lookup and records the date. Brokerage (entity) licenses in Arizona also have to be checked on the state site.

entries.title: How does AVYRO pick the best broker partner for a lead?
entries.answer: On a lead's profile (admins and owners) the Partner broker panel, and on the Referrals tab, choose a lead whose owner has given permission and AVYRO suggests the best partners. A partner is only suggested if it is active, license verified, agreement and legal review done, licensed in the lead's state, not marked do not assign, not at its maximum open leads, not flagged as having stopped reporting, and covers the lead's market, property type and budget band where those are known. The rest are shown with the reason each was ruled out. The suggestions are ranked: a city match counts most, then a county match, a budget in the middle of their band, a good update rate, earlier closes, an exclusive territory and any manual boost. If no partner qualifies, the lead is shown as needing a partner, so recruit one for that state; the owner can still be offered the NAVEO Stays path meanwhile. The state must also be switched on in the States tab before a lead can be sent.

entries.title: How do I email a partner broker about a lead, ask for a status or send the fee details?
entries.answer: Once a lead has been sent to a partner (on the lead's Partner broker panel or the Referrals tab) there are three emails, each sent only when you press its button. Email lead packet sends the partner a lead reference, the property, the owner's name and phone as permitted, the agreed fee and protection period, and how to report. It is refused if the owner's permission to share is no longer recorded or the lead is marked do not contact. Ask for a status update asks the partner for a one-line status, and can only go out once every three days. Email fee details is available when the referral is closed: it reminds the partner of the fee, the payee and the days to pay, and asks for the commission received and its date. Partners reply with the lead reference in the subject, for example Lead AZ-2026-A1B2C3, Contacted. Replies go to your own email, and you record the status on the referral. Every email is logged with its status so you can see what was sent and whether it failed. Text messages to partners are not sent from AVYRO.

entries.title: What emails do I send to recruit a broker partner, and when?
entries.answer: The Recruiting playbook on the Partners tab has the sequence ready to use. Send the first email on day 0, a short bump on day 3 and a last note on day 7, only if there has been no reply. When a broker shows interest, send the terms email with the one-page summary and the agreement, then hold a 10-minute call covering how leads are sourced, the fee (typically 25 to 30 percent of their side, paid only after they are paid at closing), status reporting and the 180-day protection period. After the call, send the agreement email; test leads go out only once the agreement is signed and their license is confirmed active in the lead's state. Pick a prospect in the playbook to fill in their name and market, add your details once, then copy the email or open it in your email app. Press Log it as sent on the prospect's card and AVYRO tracks the next step: the day-3 bump and day-7 note show when they are due, and the Follow-up due filter lists the prospects waiting on you. Nothing is sent automatically.

entries.title: How do avyropro.ai, naveohomes.com and staynaveo.com work together?
entries.answer: AVYRO (avyropro.ai) is the intelligence layer and the system of record for leads, owners, partners, consents, referrals, fees, listings, prices, availability and bookings. NAVEO Homes (naveohomes.com) is the sales and referral front end: homeowners submit a sell form, staff work leads and assign licensed partner brokerages, and partners sign in to update referrals. NAVEO Stays (staynaveo.com) is the guest booking and owner front end: guests browse live homes and book, and owners ask for a rental-management analysis. Each site keeps only what it needs to run and calls AVYRO with one shared key. The brand name is always NAVEO Stays and NAVEO Homes, never AVYRO Stays or AVYRO Homes. Partner and referral data stays with NAVEO Homes, the internal intent score never appears on a public site, and nothing about fees or partner agreements goes to NAVEO Stays.

entries.title: How do the NAVEO sites connect to AVYRO, and why would they get a 401?
entries.answer: Both NAVEO sites call AVYRO with one shared key sent as x-naveo-key. The key only works on an allowlist of routes (seller intake, owner inquiries, listings, bookings, calendar, reviews and the partner referral routes) and only inside one organization, acting as one dedicated AVYRO user. It cannot reach partner onboarding, agreements, revenue, state activation or backfills. AVYRO needs three settings: NAVEO_INTEGRATION_KEY (24 or more characters), NAVEO_ORGANIZATION_ID and NAVEO_ACTOR_USER_ID. If any is missing, or the key is wrong or short, every call returns 401. To rotate the key, set the same new value in AVYRO, NAVEO Homes and NAVEO Stays and redeploy each, then confirm a call returns 200. Never paste the key into chat or into browser code.

entries.title: What happens when a homeowner submits their property on naveohomes.com?
entries.answer: The submission creates one AVYRO lead and one open seller opportunity, and the lead id is the Lead ID on both sides; a retry with the same submission id never makes a second lead. Nothing is sent to the owner. If the follow-up box was ticked, AVYRO records that consent. The homeowner sees AVYRO's dual-path recommendation (Sell only, Sell + Earn, Rent while preparing, or Investor exit) with its reasons and cautions, and never sees the internal intent score, which is only for matching and prioritizing. A repeat submission for a property AVYRO already knows gets the on-site estimate instead of an AVYRO recommendation, so one submission never reveals what AVYRO holds about another record. On a repeat, the owner's contact name and phone overwrite the existing ones, so check before relying on the old contact.

entries.title: How does a property appear on the NAVEO Homes listings page?
entries.answer: A lead is shown on NAVEO Homes only after a person marks it listed (the naveo_listed_at field); clearing it removes the property at once. The read-only listings route returns property facts, a price and photos a person has cleared for publishing, and never owner contact details, notes or scores. It is limited to the key's own organization. Until a screen exists for the flag, it is set with a database update.

entries.title: What happens when an owner asks NAVEO Stays for a rental analysis or is referred?
entries.answer: An owner who fills in the For Owners or Contact form is saved as a NAVEO Stays lead first, so nothing is lost if AVYRO is down, then sent to AVYRO as a rental lead with an open opportunity routed to short-term-rental management, never a sale. A repeat of the same submission returns the same lead. No consent is logged unless the owner ticked the follow-up box, as on the Earn While You Sell form, which also sends homeowners here; otherwise the lead stays at needs permission until a person adds it. An owner who was referred by an existing owner did not ask for anything: AVYRO records them as Referred, Permission Needed with email opt-in off and a weak signal, and nobody contacts them until permission is recorded. The Stays forms only ask for a city or area, so a person has to find out the exact location later.

entries.title: Which homes can guests see and reserve on NAVEO Stays?
entries.answer: AVYRO owns each NAVEO Stays home: its details, photos, nightly price, cleaning fee, minimum nights, status and calendar. A home is shown and open to reservations only when its status is active, it is quality-approved and nothing recorded blocks short-term rental (a denied permit, zoning not cleared, or HOA not allowed). A draft, paused, blocked or maintenance home disappears from the site and cannot be reserved, and its page says it is no longer available. If a home is also for sale, the site shows that and its handover date, and a booking cannot end after the handover. Showing times are calendar holds, and the reasons for any hold are never shown to guests. Links using a home's old NAVEO Stays id still work.

entries.title: How does a NAVEO Stays booking work, and how are double bookings prevented?
entries.answer: When a guest books, NAVEO Stays checks the home and dates with AVYRO, then AVYRO works out the total from the listing (nights times the nightly rate plus the cleaning fee; there is no guest service fee) and creates the booking and its calendar block in one step under a lock, so two guests can never hold the same night. The database also refuses overlapping bookings as a backstop. Check-out day can be booked by the next guest. If those nights were just taken, the guest sees that the dates were just booked. NAVEO Stays keeps its own copy of the booking for confirmation emails and Rewards, and if saving that copy fails the AVYRO booking is cancelled so no nights stay held. A booking can be cancelled, which frees its dates, or completed; a cancelled booking cannot be reopened. Payment is arranged after booking.

entries.title: How do owner calendar holds, guest reviews and revenue reporting work for NAVEO Stays?
entries.answer: Owners and staff can hold dates for owner use, maintenance or other reasons; a hold is refused if any of those nights is already booked, and only owner, maintenance and other holds can be removed that way. Showing holds are set by AVYRO staff. A guest review is tied to a booking reference, one review per booking, and updates the home's public rating and review count. Revenue and occupancy for a home over a date window are computed from AVYRO's own bookings: revenue counts a booking in the window its check-in falls in, and booked nights are clipped to the window. Owners use the owner page on NAVEO Stays and guests use the review page opened from the emailed link, which goes out in the thank-you email after checkout. That email is sent by a daily job (15:00 UTC) that AVYRO's scheduler starts, because the Stays platform cannot schedule it itself.

entries.title: What are the first steps to prove the NAVEO Homes and NAVEO Stays loops with real data?
entries.answer: Prove two loops with real data before scaling. Homes: a real homeowner submits, the lead appears in AVYRO with its Lead ID, a licensed partner is assigned only after the owner authorizes the introduction, and the partner moves it to Contacted, with status history in AVYRO. Stays: a real home is imported or created in AVYRO, marked active and quality-approved with the correct price and photos, shows on staynaveo.com, its dates check against the calendar, and a booking is written back to AVYRO. Then sign one or two licensed partners in the strongest market, assign the first real leads the day the first partner signs, and watch assigned, contacted, listed, bookings and expected fees weekly. Add a second partner in a market only after the first reports reliably, and open a new market only with a signed partner and live Stays inventory.

entries.title: How do owners see only their own homes and submissions on NAVEO Homes and NAVEO Stays?
entries.answer: Owner access is decided in AVYRO by matching the email an owner signs in with to the owner_email stored on the home or submission, always lowercase and exact (no partial or domain matching). If owner_email is empty, no owner can open it. On NAVEO Stays, owner_email is on each listing, so a signed-in owner sees only their own homes and can hold dates, see bookings and revenue, and pause or resume bookings; someone else's home, or one that does not exist, looks the same (not found). On NAVEO Homes, owner_email is set when a homeowner submits their own property, and their submission page shows only the property, where it stands, the recommendation they were shown and the name of the partner introduced. It never shows the internal intent score, fee terms, or partner and broker notes. A repeat submission for a property AVYRO already holds does not open the existing entry: it is treated as an ownership claim, the submitter sees only that it was received, and a person compares the address and approves or dismisses it in the Owner access tab of Seller & owner services. The check runs on every request, not just at sign-in. Staff set each Stays home's owner email, and any co-owner or manager emails (up to 10) that may also manage it, in the Owner access tab; the old email loses access at once.

entries.title: How is the Prospect Score calculated?
entries.answer: The Prospect Score is a 0 to 100 number on every lead that says how good a short-term-rental prospect it is and how ready it is to contact. It is not a seller-intent score. Five factors are each scored 0 to 100 and weighted: Revenue Potential 25, Property Fit 25, Regulatory Feasibility 25, Lead Quality 15, and Engagement and Freshness 10 (weights can be changed in the score weight editor). Revenue Potential uses estimated monthly net income, preferring AirDNA's own figure, then the stored estimate, then the listed rent or a rent estimate for a sale listing; a sale price never counts as income. Property Fit rewards 3 to 5 bedrooms, 2 or more baths, houses and townhomes, furnished and luxury homes, and penalizes apartment communities. Regulatory Feasibility is Allowed 100, Restricted 70, Pending 35, Unknown 25, and Prohibited or Banned 0. Lead Quality rewards a verified owner, a verified address, a usable phone, an email and a skip-trace match. Engagement rewards replies, callbacks, link clicks, answered calls, a submitted estimate form and fresh listings, and fades as the last activity ages. The raw total is stretched so 60 raw becomes about 75, then capped when key data is missing, floored to 80 or higher for a lead who replied or asked for a call (the floor fades with silence), and capped at 30 if they declined. Do Not Contact, a prohibited market or a terminal stage blocks the lead. Bands: Hot 80 or more, Warm 60 to 79, Nurture 40 to 59, Cold below 40, and Blocked. The model version is stored with each score so it can be recomputed when the formula changes.

entries.title: How is seller intent scored, and who sees it?
entries.answer: Seller intent is a separate 0 to 100 number, stored as intent_score on a seller opportunity. It is for internal prioritizing and partner matching and is never shown to homeowners. For a text or email reply it is read from the words: each explicit sentence about selling (wants to sell, considering a sale, putting it on the market, asked for an offer or value, asked about a buyer) adds 45; if there is none, a mention of selling or a broker adds 20; a life change such as retiring, downsizing or relocating adds 10; a stated timeline adds 15. A reply that says they are not selling scores nothing. A NAVEO Homes sell-form submission is an explicit signal and starts at 70, plus 10 for a plan to sell within 3 months and 5 for a phone number. A NAVEO Stays owner inquiry starts at 60 as a rental-management request, plus 5 for a phone and 5 if they already self-manage or use a manager. An owner who was only referred is a weak signal at 35. On a repeat signal the opportunity keeps the higher score. A separate service fit score is the best match among the services AVYRO suggests (a sale partner scores 85 for explicit intent and 45 for possible intent). Neither number is a prediction that a home will sell, and a person always decides the route.

entries.title: Does AVYRO have an automated valuation (AVM) or an AVM confidence score?
entries.answer: AVYRO does not run a sale-value AVM and has no AVM confidence score for property value. The estimates it does hold are different. Rent: for sale listings it replaces the market-average rent with RentCast's long-term rent estimate for the property (an AVM for rent, not value), highest-scoring leads first and capped by a monthly request budget. That lead is marked HIGH confidence when the estimate's low-to-high range is within 40 percent of the rent, MEDIUM otherwise, and a lookup with no answer is marked as a miss so it is not retried every run. Short-term income: AirDNA supplies daily rate, occupancy, annual revenue and its own confidence level, and the Prospect Score treats 65 percent of AirDNA annual revenue, divided by 12, as net monthly income. Seller net proceeds in the dual-path analysis come from the price the owner says they expect minus selling costs (7 percent by default), and it says plainly that this is the owner's expectation, not a valuation or comparable sales. The NAVEO Homes site's own estimate before AVYRO answers is a simple price-per-square-foot calculation by market and condition with a fixed band of about 4 percent each way, not a model with a confidence score. None of these is an appraisal, an offer or a promise.

entries.title: Where does AVYRO get listing and property data, and does it send anything back to Zillow or the MLS?
entries.answer: AVYRO only reads listing data and never sends anything to Zillow, the MLS or any portal. Listings arrive from Zillow, PadMapper and HotPads through a data provider's API, from Trulia through its own ingestion, from Craigslist and other portals, and from manual and master CSV uploads. Each lead keeps its source label (Zillow, HotPads, Trulia, Redfin, Airbnb, VRBO, MLS, Direct and others). MLS is only a label for rows loaded from licensed sources; the code has no direct MLS feed connector. Rent and income figures come from RentCast and AirDNA, and owner phone and email from skip-trace and PropertyReach style enrichment. A listing on Zillow with no agent or broker, or marked as a Zillow Rentals listing, is treated as owner-listed. Source pulls report when a source is unavailable instead of silently returning zero, never create made-up properties, and never move a lead's pipeline stage. Once a property is a lead, referrals, bookings and status live in AVYRO. Use of any portal or MLS data must follow that source's licence and display terms.

entries.title: How does AVYRO choose between Sell only, Sell + Earn, Rent while preparing and Investor exit?
entries.answer: The recommendation comes from fixed, deliberately cautious rules, checked in this order, so a person can see why and correct it. Investor exit: the home already runs as a short-term rental or the owner is open to buyers who want income. Sell only: a tenant lives there; the owner needs to sell right away (under a month); short-term rentals are restricted or prohibited; the rules are not confirmed; there is no net income estimate to compare; or the home is already listed or under contract. Otherwise, when rentals are allowed and there is an estimated interim net, it is Rent while preparing for an owner with six months or more who has not listed, and Sell + Earn for everyone else. Interim net is the estimated monthly net income times the months available before the sale. The sale side uses the owner's price expectation less selling costs (default 7 percent) and a default 90 days to sell until a person enters real figures, and it says when defaults are used. It always notes that net proceeds are the owner's expectation, not a valuation. The result is an estimate to plan the conversation, not an offer to buy, sell or rent, and it never sets the service route by itself.
